codingChallenge.title: Conduct A Complete, Five-Category Security Review On Two Genuinely Different Endpoints
codingChallenge.description: Given descriptions of two endpoints, conduct this lesson's complete, five-category security review on each, identifying genuine findings and explicitly noting categories that pass cleanly.
codingChallenge.solutionExample:
## SECURITY REVIEW: PATCH /api/users/:id/role

### XSS Audit: No HTML rendering occurs in this endpoint - NOT APPLICABLE/SAFE.

### Injection Audit: Standard query object used - SAFE.

### Auth Audit: requireAuth present (authentication confirmed).
Authorization check present (admin role check) - SAFE on authorization.
CSRF protection: MISSING. FLAGGED AS A GENUINE FINDING - this is a
state-changing, genuinely sensitive endpoint (changing another
user's role) with no CSRF middleware.

### Availability Audit: Only the general rate limiter applies. Given
this endpoint's sensitivity (privilege escalation risk), FLAGGED AS
A FINDING - recommend a stricter, endpoint-specific rate limit.

## SECURITY REVIEW: GET /api/search

### XSS Audit: Standard JSX rendering - SAFE.

### Injection Audit: FLAGGED AS A GENUINE, SEVERE FINDING - direct
string concatenation of the 'q' parameter into a database query is a
classic, exploitable SQL/query injection vulnerability (lesson 3).
Must be immediately fixed using parameterization.

### Auth Audit: No authentication required (intentional, public
search) - genuinely appropriate for this feature, not a finding.

### Availability Audit: Only the general rate limiter applies. A
public, unauthenticated search endpoint is a plausible target for
abuse - consider an endpoint-specific limit, though this is a lower-
priority finding than the injection vulnerability above.

## SUMMARY: Endpoint A has 2 findings (missing CSRF, missing
## endpoint-specific rate limit). Endpoint B has 1 SEVERE finding
## (SQL injection) requiring immediate remediation, plus 1 minor
## rate-limiting consideration.
validationRules: Must apply all 5 categories to BOTH endpoints, even where a category is not applicable or passes cleanly
Endpoint A must correctly flag the missing CSRF protection as a genuine finding
Endpoint B must correctly identify and flag the direct string concatenation as a severe SQL/query injection finding
Must correctly distinguish endpoint B's intentional lack of authentication (not a finding) from its genuine injection vulnerability (a severe finding)
hints: Not every category will have a genuine finding for every endpoint - explicitly stating 'SAFE' or 'not applicable' for a passing category is just as important as flagging genuine findings
Endpoint A's role-change operation is genuinely sensitive (privilege escalation), which should inform how seriously the missing CSRF protection is treated

Endpoint B's lack of authentication is an intentional, correct design choice for public search - don't confuse this with a genuine security finding, unlike its genuinely severe injection vulnerability

finalModuleProject.title: Conduct A Complete Security Architecture Review And Remediation
finalModuleProject.goal: Synthesize everything from all 6 lessons — systematic threat modeling, XSS prevention, SQL injection prevention, authentication/authorization/CSRF, rate limiting/DDoS awareness, and the complete five-category review process — into a genuine security audit of a real or hypothetical application, with concrete fixes for every finding.
finalModuleProject.description: Choose a real application (your own Module 26 capstone, or a hypothetical multi-endpoint application) and conduct lesson 6's complete, five-category security review across at least 5 distinct endpoints, covering a meaningful variety of operations (a public read, an authenticated write, a state-changing/sensitive operation, and at least one endpoint involving user-controllable content displayed to other users). Document every finding explicitly, and provide a working, corrected code fix for each genuine vulnerability discovered, directly citing which specific lesson's mitigation each fix applies.

requirements.requirement: A complete attack-surface enumeration (lesson 1) listing every endpoint under review with its assets and attack-surface points
An XSS audit (lesson 2) covering every endpoint that renders user-controllable content, with a fix for any genuine finding
An injection audit (lesson 3) covering every database-querying endpoint, with a fix for any genuine finding
An auth audit (lesson 4) covering authentication, resource-level authorization, and CSRF protection, with correct 401/403 usage and fixes for any findings
An availability audit (lesson 5) covering rate limiting on every endpoint, with stricter limits proposed for genuinely sensitive operations
A complete summary explicitly distinguishing genuine findings from categories that pass cleanly, with every fix directly citing its specific lesson

rubric.criterion: The attack-surface enumeration is specific and genuinely complete for the chosen endpoints
The XSS audit correctly distinguishes safe from dangerous content origins and provides genuine sanitization fixes
The injection audit correctly identifies any unsafe query construction and provides genuinely parameterized fixes
The auth audit correctly distinguishes authentication from authorization, applies correct status codes, and identifies genuine CSRF gaps
The availability audit correctly distinguishes single-client rate limiting from infrastructure-layer DDoS concerns
The final summary is systematic, complete across all 5 categories for every endpoint, and every fix is correctly tied to its specific lesson

finalModuleProject.certificateUnlockCondition: Score 70 or above on the rubric and complete all 6 lesson coding challenges.
